q: After a workstation compromise, an attacker moved freely to servers across the same flat internal network. Which architectural change BEST limits this lateral movement in the future?
c: Deploying a stronger firewall at the Internet edge
Enforcing longer passwords on all workstations
Segmenting the network and restricting traffic between zones
Increasing logging on the core switches

q: In a three-tier web application exposed to the Internet, where should the database server be positioned?
c: In an internal zone reachable only from the application tier
In the DMZ alongside the public web servers
On the public subnet behind a host firewall
On the same VLAN as user workstations

q: Users on an office VLAN intermittently receive network settings from an unauthorized device, which routes their traffic through an attacker-controlled gateway. Which switch feature MOST directly prevents this?
c: Port security limiting MAC addresses per port
DHCP snooping with trusted ports
Spanning Tree Protocol root guard
802.1X port-based network access control

q: Two branch offices must protect all traffic exchanged between their networks across the Internet, including concealing the original internal IP headers. Which configuration meets this requirement?
c: IPsec ESP in transport mode between the gateways
IPsec AH in tunnel mode between the sites
TLS on each application crossing the link
IPsec ESP in tunnel mode between the site gateways

q: Remote employees reach corporate systems through a VPN, while their other web traffic bypasses the tunnel and goes straight to the Internet. What is the PRIMARY security concern with this split-tunnel arrangement?
c: Encryption strength drops when the tunnel is split
Split tunnels consume extra VPN bandwidth
The device can bridge Internet threats into the corporate network
Users lose access to internal resources

q: A utility connects its plant control network to the corporate IT network for production reporting, but engineering workstations must never be directly reachable from the business side. Which design BEST enforces this?
c: A brokered intermediary zone that terminates all cross-boundary flows
Separate VLANs for IT and OT on the shared core switches
Host-based firewalls on each engineering workstation
Encryption of all traffic passing between IT and OT

q: A security analyst discovers that an attacker on a user-facing access port sent traffic into a restricted VLAN by crafting frames with two 802.1Q tags. Which switch configuration change BEST prevents this double-tagging attack?
c: Enable dynamic trunking negotiation on all access ports so the switch controls trunk formation
Assign the native VLAN on trunk links to an unused VLAN ID and hard-code user ports as access ports
Configure DHCP snooping so untrusted ports cannot deliver tagged frames into the network
Apply port mirroring to copy access-port traffic to a monitoring VLAN for inspection

q: A hospital wants to ensure that only managed, corporate-owned devices can connect to wired network ports in public waiting areas, where visitors can physically reach the jacks. Which control BEST meets this requirement?
c: MAC address filtering maintained on each access switch
Placing all waiting-area ports in a guest VLAN with Internet-only access
802.1X port-based authentication using certificates issued to corporate devices
Physically locking network jacks and disabling all unused wall ports

q: A small office currently uses WPA2-Personal with a shared passphrase on its wireless network. The owner asks what security benefit an upgrade to WPA3-Personal would provide. Which improvement is MOST significant?
c: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals resists offline dictionary attacks against captured handshakes
It replaces the shared passphrase with per-user credentials tied to a RADIUS server
It introduces AES encryption, which WPA2 did not support
It hides the SSID so attackers can no longer discover the network name

q: An external scan shows a customer-facing payment portal still accepts TLS 1.0 connections for legacy browser compatibility, though analytics show fewer than 0.1 percent of clients use it. As security manager, what should you recommend FIRST?
c: Deploy a web application firewall rule to inspect TLS 1.0 sessions for attack signatures
Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on the portal after a short notice period to the residual client base
Direct the application team to migrate every internal service to TLS 1.3 simultaneously
Accept the risk formally, since fewer than 0.1 percent of connections are affected

q: A SaaS provider's traffic was briefly routed through an unrelated foreign network after another autonomous system announced a more specific BGP prefix covering the provider's address space. Which measure BEST reduces the chance of a recurrence?
c: Enable MD5 authentication on all BGP peering sessions with adjacent providers
Require TLS for all customer connections so intercepted traffic remains unreadable
Publish route origin authorizations for its prefixes and use transit providers that drop RPKI-invalid announcements
Advertise more specific prefixes continuously so competing announcements never win best-path selection

q: After a DNS cache-poisoning incident redirected employees to a counterfeit payroll portal, an architect proposes deploying DNSSEC validation on the enterprise resolvers. Which outcome should management expect this control to deliver?
c: Queries and responses will be encrypted, hiding employees' lookups from eavesdroppers
Known-malicious domains will be blocked through signed reputation feeds
Zone transfers will require mutually authenticated TLS sessions between servers
Resolvers will be able to verify that answers are authentic and unmodified via digital signatures

q: A company adopting zero trust currently grants full intranet access to any device that connects through the campus LAN or the VPN. Which core principle should the new architecture apply in place of this assumption?
c: Access decisions must be made per session based on identity, device posture, and context rather than network location
All internal traffic must be blocked until the perimeter firewall is replaced with a next-generation model
Users on the corporate LAN may retain implicit trust while only VPN users are continuously re-authenticated
Encrypting all internal traffic between endpoints is sufficient to establish trust

q: A team configured an IPsec VPN to a partner using Authentication Header, but the tunnel fails whenever traffic passes through the branch office's NAT gateway. The partner also requires confidentiality for the data. What should the team do?
c: Replace the NAT gateway with static one-to-one address mappings so AH integrity checks remain valid
Switch AH from tunnel mode to transport mode so the outer header is no longer protected
Use ESP with NAT traversal, which provides integrity and confidentiality and tolerates address translation
Encapsulate the AH tunnel inside GRE so the translated header is hidden from the integrity check

q: A retailer is replacing its MPLS circuits with SD-WAN that sends branch traffic over local broadband Internet links, including direct breakout to cloud applications. Which consideration is MOST important for the security architecture?
c: Preserving MPLS-equivalent quality of service so voice and video traffic does not degrade
Ensuring branch routers have capacity to carry full Internet BGP routing tables
Consolidating branch firewalls into the SD-WAN controller, which now centrally enforces all policy
Protecting traffic that now rides the public Internet with authenticated encrypted tunnels and inspection at cloud breakout points

q: Finance staff keep receiving convincing invoice emails that spoof the company's own domain in the visible From header. SPF is already published. Which addition BEST enables receiving servers to reject these forged messages?
c: Publish a DMARC reject policy with DKIM signing so receivers verify alignment with the visible From domain
Tighten the SPF record to a hard-fail qualifier so unauthorized sending hosts are refused
Deploy S/MIME certificates to all finance employees so their outbound mail is digitally signed
Enable opportunistic TLS between mail gateways to stop interception of messages in transit

q: A company deploying VoIP wants to keep the audio content of calls confidential as it crosses the office network. Which protocol is specifically designed to provide this protection?
c: SIP over TLS
RTP
SRTP

q: An HVAC vendor needs recurring remote access to maintenance servers on the facilities network. Today a technician connects through a shared desktop-sharing tool installed on an engineer's workstation. Which redesign BEST manages this third-party connectivity?
c: Issue the vendor a standard employee VPN profile so sessions traverse the corporate remote access concentrator
Route vendor sessions through a dedicated jump host with MFA, individual accounts, session recording, and access scoped to the maintenance servers
Keep the desktop-sharing tool but restrict its use to business hours through firewall schedules
Require the vendor to sign a connection agreement documenting their security obligations and liability

q: An online brokerage's 10 Gbps Internet links were saturated for hours by a 300 Gbps reflection flood; on-premises appliances never saw manageable load. Management asks how to withstand a repeat event. Which approach is MOST effective?
c: Upgrade the perimeter firewalls to higher-throughput models with SYN flood protection features
Implement rate limiting and geographic blocking ACLs on the enterprise border routers
Increase Internet capacity to 40 Gbps spread across redundant carriers and diverse paths
Engage an upstream cloud scrubbing or CDN-based mitigation service that filters attack traffic before it reaches the enterprise links

q: During an incident investigation, analysts find timestamps across firewalls, servers, and domain controllers differ by minutes, and one syslog source is hours off, making event correlation unreliable. Which design change BEST prevents this problem?
c: Configure each device to poll any public NTP pool server of its administrator's choosing
Synchronize device clocks manually during quarterly maintenance windows
Deploy a redundant internal time hierarchy traceable to trusted references, with authenticated NTP required for all logging devices
Compensate in the SIEM by applying a per-source clock offset to timestamps as events are ingested

q: A firewall protecting a cardholder-data enclave suffers a software crash. By design, no traffic may pass while the device is down, even though this interrupts business transactions until service is restored. Which principle does this design illustrate?
c: Fail secure (fail closed)
Fail open
Graceful degradation
High availability

q: An internal HR web application must become reachable to employees on the Internet without exposing the application server directly. The architect wants external connections terminated in a controlled zone, with inspection and authentication applied before requests reach the internal server. Which component fits this design?
c: A forward proxy configured in employees' browser settings
A NAT rule on the perimeter firewall publishing the server's internal address
A site-to-site VPN concentrator linking employees' home networks to the datacenter
A reverse proxy in a screened subnet that relays validated requests to the internal application

q: Penetration testers stood up a rogue access point broadcasting the corporate SSID and harvested employees' 802.1X credentials when laptops attempted to authenticate through it. Which control BEST prevents corporate devices from disclosing credentials to such an evil twin?
c: Configure supplicants to validate the RADIUS server certificate against a pinned trusted CA and refuse authentication otherwise
Reduce access point transmit power so the corporate wireless signal does not extend beyond the building
Enforce a longer and more complex password policy for all wireless network users
Enable MAC address filtering so only corporate laptops can associate with the wireless network

q: Monitoring alerts that a switch's MAC address table filled with tens of thousands of entries learned from one access port, and the switch began flooding unicast frames out all ports, letting a connected host capture other users' traffic. Which control directly counters this attack?
c: Storm control thresholds for broadcast and multicast traffic volumes
Port security limiting the number of source MAC addresses learned per port
BPDU guard to shut down ports that receive spanning tree protocol messages
Dynamic ARP inspection validating address resolution messages on untrusted ports

q: A network engineer proposes that switch, router, and firewall administration interfaces be reachable only from a physically separate management network rather than from the production LAN. What is the PRIMARY security benefit of this design?
c: It increases throughput by removing management traffic from busy production links
It lets administrators manage devices conveniently from any workstation in the enterprise
A compromised production host cannot reach device management planes, and administration remains possible during production network incidents
It eliminates the need for authentication on device interfaces since the management network is isolated

q: Two internal microservices exchange sensitive account data across the datacenter network. Policy requires that each service verify the identity of the other before any data flows, in addition to encrypting the session. Which mechanism satisfies both requirements?
c: TLS with server certificates issued by the internal certificate authority
Mutual TLS in which each service presents and validates a certificate during the handshake
IP allowlists restricting which datacenter hosts may open connections to each service
Hashing each payload with SHA-256 before it is transmitted between the services

q: A company carries iSCSI storage traffic across the same converged datacenter network as ordinary server VLANs to reduce cabling costs. An auditor flags the design as exposing block storage to any compromised server. Which combination of measures BEST addresses the risk?
c: Enable jumbo frames and QoS tagging so storage traffic receives priority over user traffic
Isolate storage traffic on dedicated non-routed VLANs or a separate fabric, and require mutual CHAP authentication between initiators and targets
Replace iSCSI with Fibre Channel, since a dedicated FC fabric is immune to network-based attacks
Encrypt data at rest on the storage arrays so intercepted LUN traffic is unreadable to attackers

q: An IPv4-only enterprise discovers workstations exfiltrating data through tunnels established after receiving rogue IPv6 router advertisements on the LAN, bypassing egress controls that inspect only IPv4. Which action BEST remediates this exposure?
c: Block protocol 41 encapsulation at the Internet perimeter so IPv6 packets cannot leave inside IPv4
Rely on the existing NAT boundary, since private internal addressing prevents hosts from reaching external tunnel endpoints
Enable RA Guard on access ports and bring IPv6 within egress policy and monitoring, disabling it where it is not needed
Deploy intrusion detection signatures that alert on traffic patterns of known IPv6 tunneling utilities

q: A SOC relies on internal DNS resolver logs to detect malware command-and-control domains. Detections are dropping because many endpoints and browsers now resolve names via encrypted DNS over HTTPS directly to public providers. What should the security team do FIRST?
c: Decrypt all outbound HTTPS at the forward proxy so encrypted DNS queries become visible again
Accept encrypted DNS as a privacy improvement and retire the DNS-based detection content
Migrate detection to flow-record analysis, which does not depend on observing name resolution
Use endpoint and browser policy to direct managed devices to the enterprise resolver and block known external DoH services at egress

q: A board meeting held on the company's video conferencing platform was joined by an uninvited participant who obtained the reusable meeting link from a forwarded email. Which combination of platform controls BEST prevents a recurrence for sensitive meetings?
c: Unique per-meeting links with authenticated join, waiting-room admission, and locking the session once attendees arrive
End-to-end encryption so the meeting's audio and video streams cannot be read in transit
Recording every sensitive session so any intrusion can be identified and reviewed afterward
A published policy stating that links for sensitive meetings must never be forwarded

q: Two campus buildings are connected by a provider-delivered metro Ethernet circuit operating at layer 2. Security requires line-rate encryption of all traffic between the buildings, including non-IP protocols, with minimal added latency. Which technology BEST fits?
c: Site-to-site IPsec tunnels between routers placed at each building
MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) enabled on the switch interfaces facing the metro Ethernet link
TLS enforced for every application communicating across the inter-building link
PPTP tunnels established between the campus core switches at each site

q: During an architecture review, a network engineer argues that a branch office does not need a firewall because all hosts use RFC 1918 private addresses behind NAT, so outsiders cannot reach them anyway. What is the BEST response from the security architect?
c: Agree, because NAT hides internal addresses and drops unsolicited inbound packets by design
Require proxy ARP on the edge router to conceal internal MAC addresses from the Internet
Explain that NAT is an address translation mechanism, not a security control, and require a firewall enforcing explicit policy
Replace NAT with IPv6 global addressing so IPsec can be used end to end without translation

q: An audit finds that administrators manage core switches over Telnet from their desktops, so device credentials cross the network in cleartext. Which remediation should the security team recommend FIRST?
c: Replace Telnet with SSH for all device management sessions
Enable SNMPv3 on the switches for configuration changes
Require administrators to change device passwords after every session
Move the switches to a separate VLAN so users cannot reach them

q: A legal team must email highly sensitive case files to outside counsel. The email gateway already negotiates opportunistic TLS with most partner domains. Why might the security officer still require S/MIME encryption for these messages?
c: TLS cannot encrypt attachments larger than the negotiated record size
TLS protects mail only between servers, while S/MIME keeps content encrypted end to end, including on relays and in mailboxes
S/MIME provides faster delivery because encrypted messages bypass content inspection at every relaying gateway
Opportunistic TLS always downgrades to cleartext when either mail server also supports S/MIME

q: Penetration testers repeatedly exploit SQL injection in a public web application over HTTPS. Code fixes will take months to ship. Which network control BEST reduces this exposure in the meantime?
c: A stateful packet-filtering firewall restricting inbound traffic to TCP port 443
A network intrusion prevention system watching the encrypted sessions inline
A screened subnet separating the web tier from the database tier
A web application firewall terminating TLS and filtering application-layer requests

q: Your company acquires a smaller firm, and executives want the two office networks fully joined within a week to speed integration. The acquired network's security posture is unknown. What should the security architect recommend FIRST?
c: Connect the networks only through a restrictive, monitored interconnect while the acquired environment is assessed
Merge the networks immediately and schedule a vulnerability scan of the acquired hosts for the following quarter
Extend the corporate zero trust policy engine across the acquired firm before allowing any connectivity
Require the acquired firm to re-address its network into the corporate IP plan before any traffic is exchanged

q: A security team notices its IDS misses sessions during peak hours. The sensor receives traffic from a switch SPAN port that is frequently oversubscribed. What is the BEST way to give the sensor complete visibility?
c: Configure an additional SPAN session on the same switch to share the mirroring load
Deploy a dedicated network TAP on the monitored link and feed the sensor from it
Move the sensor inline so the switch must forward every packet through it
Enable NetFlow export so the sensor can reconstruct the missing sessions

q: A hotel wants guests to join Wi-Fi without accounts or passwords, but a review found the current open SSID lets anyone eavesdrop on guest traffic. Which option BEST addresses the eavesdropping while preserving the frictionless join experience?
c: Publish a shared WPA2-Personal passphrase on lobby signage so every guest device can encrypt its traffic
Add a captive portal so guests must accept terms before their traffic is allowed to flow
Enable Wi-Fi Enhanced Open (OWE) so each guest session is individually encrypted without authentication
Hide the SSID so only guests who are told the network name can associate

q: A configuration review shows routers and switches answer SNMP read and write requests using the community string 'private' from any source address. Which remediation BEST addresses the risk?
c: Change the community string to a long random value stored in the password vault
Disable SNMP entirely and rely on syslog for all device monitoring needs
Restrict SNMP to the management VLAN while keeping version 2c for tool compatibility
Migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy, and restrict sources to management hosts

q: An external assessment reveals that the company's Internet-facing DNS server answers queries for internal hostnames, exposing the names and addresses of domain controllers and file servers. Which design change BEST corrects this?
c: Implement split DNS so external servers host only public records and internal zones stay on internal resolvers
Sign all zones with DNSSEC so external parties cannot read the internal records
Block TCP port 53 at the firewall so only small UDP queries reach the server
Rename internal hosts with unpredictable labels so leaked records reveal nothing useful

q: Threat intelligence indicates an adversary is recording the company's encrypted VPN traffic for later analysis, and the concentrator's private key could plausibly be stolen in the future. Which property MOST directly limits the damage from that scenario?
c: Longer RSA keys on the concentrator certificate to make factoring computationally infeasible
Forward secrecy from ephemeral key agreement, so past sessions cannot be decrypted with the stolen key
Certificate pinning on clients so a stolen key cannot be used to impersonate the gateway
Rotating the concentrator certificate quarterly so any stolen key ages out quickly

q: A manufacturer is cabling a new production floor filled with large motors and welding equipment. Data errors from electrical interference are a major concern, and cable runs pass through areas open to visiting contractors. Which transmission medium BEST fits these conditions?
c: Shielded twisted pair, because grounding the shield eliminates all induced noise
Coaxial cable, because its solid core resists vibration from heavy machinery
Fiber optic cable, because it is immune to electromagnetic interference and difficult to tap unnoticed
Unshielded twisted pair at a higher category rating, because faster cable rejects interference

q: A hospital's 802.1X deployment cannot cover infusion pumps and badge printers that lack supplicant support, so those switch ports use MAC Authentication Bypass. The CISO asks how the risk MAB introduces should be handled. What is the BEST response?
c: MAB is equivalent to certificate authentication because the RADIUS server validates each MAC address
Disable MAB and leave those ports unauthenticated since the devices are trusted medical equipment
Replace every non-supplicant device immediately regardless of clinical replacement cycles
Keep MAB but place those devices in tightly restricted VLANs with ACLs and monitor for MAC spoofing

q: A company plans to deploy TLS interception on its web proxy to inspect outbound traffic for data loss and malware. The privacy officer raises concerns about employees' personal banking and health sites. What is the BEST way to proceed?
c: Inspect by default but bypass decryption for defined categories such as financial and health sites, and disclose the practice to employees
Inspect all traffic uniformly because selective bypass would create blind spots attackers could exploit
Abandon interception and rely on DNS-based filtering so employee content is never decrypted
Inspect all traffic but retain decrypted content for only thirty days to limit privacy exposure

q: Twice this month the network went down after employees plugged unmanaged desktop switches into wall jacks, triggering spanning tree recalculations and a bridging loop. Which control BEST prevents a recurrence at the access layer?
c: Increase the core switches' spanning tree priority so they always remain the root bridge
Enable BPDU Guard on access ports so any port receiving bridge protocol messages is shut down
Enable port security so ports that learn more than one MAC address are disabled
Deploy DHCP snooping so devices behind rogue switches cannot obtain addresses

q: An enterprise is moving its data center to a software-defined network in which a central controller programs all switching behavior through southbound APIs. During threat modeling, which risk should receive the HIGHEST priority?
c: Loss of a single leaf switch, because SDN cannot reroute around failed hardware
Encrypted east-west traffic, because inspection tools cannot read flows between virtual machines
Compromise of the controller or its APIs, because it would grant an attacker authority over the entire network's forwarding behavior
Vendor lock-in from proprietary northbound applications, because migration costs would rise

q: An office of 300 staff uses one WPA2-Personal passphrase for the corporate SSID. After several departures the passphrase has never changed, because updating every device is disruptive. Which change BEST resolves the underlying problem?
c: Adopt a longer passphrase and rotate it every ninety days through the MDM platform
Move the corporate network to a hidden SSID so former employees cannot find it
Enable MAC address filtering so only inventoried corporate devices can associate
Migrate to WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise so each user authenticates individually and access ends when accounts are disabled

q: During an external scan, testers download the company's entire DNS zone using an AXFR request against the authoritative name server, revealing every registered host. What is the BEST corrective action?
c: Restrict zone transfers to the specific addresses of authorized secondary name servers
Disable recursion on the authoritative server so it answers only for its own zones
Shorten the zone's TTL values so any leaked records expire quickly
Place the name server behind a load balancer so AXFR sessions cannot complete

q: A defense contractor sends sensitive traffic between two sites over a carrier service advertised as fully encrypted. The security architect learns each carrier node decrypts and re-encrypts traffic as it forwards it. What is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
c: The design is acceptable because traffic is never exposed on any physical wire between nodes
Link encryption leaves plaintext exposed inside intermediate nodes, so the contractor should add end-to-end encryption it controls
The carrier should be asked to add a second layer of link encryption at each hop for defense in depth
The design fails only if the carrier's nodes are located outside the contractor's home country

q: A hospital plans to deploy an inline IPS on the network segment carrying real-time patient telemetry. Engineers must choose the appliance's behavior if it loses power or crashes. Which configuration BEST reflects sound risk management?
c: Fail closed, because blocking all traffic during a failure prevents any attack from passing uninspected
Fail closed, but issue clinicians a procedure to physically re-cable around the appliance during outages
Fail open with a hardware bypass, because interrupting patient telemetry poses a greater risk than briefly uninspected traffic
Fail open permanently by running the sensor in passive SPAN mode so it can never affect traffic

q: An ISP notifies a company that packets bearing other organizations' source addresses are leaving its network as part of a reflection DDoS campaign. Which control at the Internet edge BEST prevents the company's network from being misused this way?
c: Inbound rate limiting on the border router to blunt reflected replies arriving from the campaign
Blackhole routing that discards all traffic destined for the DDoS victims' address ranges
RPKI route origin validation so forged BGP announcements are rejected at the border
Egress filtering that drops outbound packets whose source addresses are not from the company's assigned ranges

q: A quarterly review finds a firewall rule permitting any source to any destination on all ports, added during a troubleshooting session eight months earlier and forgotten. What does this finding MOST clearly indicate is missing?
c: A change management process with expiration and periodic recertification of firewall rules
A next-generation firewall, since legacy platforms cannot express granular policies
An intrusion prevention system to compensate for the overly permissive rule
Separation of duties so firewall administrators cannot approve their own emergency changes

q: Facilities installs a point-to-point wireless bridge to link two office buildings across a public street, replacing a leased line. What additional safeguard is MOST important before carrying corporate traffic over the bridge?
c: Narrow-beam directional antennas so the signal cannot be received away from the path
Strong encryption of all traffic crossing the bridge, since the radio signal extends beyond company control
MAC address filtering so only the two bridge radios can associate with each other
Reduced transmit power so the link cannot be detected from street level

q: Security policy forbids unauthorized wireless access points, but a walkthrough discovered an employee-installed AP wired into a conference room jack. Management wants continuous detection rather than periodic walkthroughs. Which control BEST meets that goal?
c: Quarterly wireless penetration tests covering every office location
A NAC agent on corporate laptops that reports nearby SSIDs to a central console
A wireless intrusion prevention system with sensors that continuously scan for rogue devices
An annual review of switch CAM tables for unrecognized MAC addresses

q: Weeks after moving to SIP trunking, a company receives a massive bill for international calls placed overnight through its IP-PBX. Investigation finds Internet-exposed SIP registration protected only by weak extension passwords. Which combination MOST effectively prevents recurrence?
c: Enable SRTP on all calls so attackers cannot listen to the fraudulent conversations
Move the PBX behind NAT so external endpoints can no longer send packets to it
Publish the trunk on a nonstandard port so scanners stop finding the registration service
Restrict signaling to the provider's addresses, enforce strong authentication over TLS, and set toll restrictions with alerts

q: A retailer offloads its storefront to a CDN that terminates TLS at global edge nodes. An architect discovers the CDN fetches content from the origin data center over plain HTTP because that connection is considered trusted. What is the MOST significant issue?
c: Customers' browsers will display certificate warnings because the edge certificate does not match the origin
CDN caching will serve stale pages because HTTP responses cannot carry cache-control headers
Traffic between the CDN edge and the origin crosses the Internet unencrypted, exposing sessions and data despite the padlock users see
TLS termination at the edge violates PCI DSS, which requires encryption to terminate only inside the cardholder environment

q: A regional branch office uses consumer-grade wireless access points. During an assessment, testers recover the Wi-Fi passphrase in a few hours without capturing any authentication handshakes, by brute-forcing an eight-digit setup PIN exposed by a push-button convenience feature. Which action BEST eliminates this attack path?
c: Replace the passphrase with a much longer randomly generated one
Enable MAC address filtering so only known adapters can associate
Disable Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) on every access point
Lower the transmit power so the signal does not reach the parking lot

q: Users on a switched office VLAN report intermittent browser certificate warnings. Investigators find a workstation broadcasting gratuitous ARP replies that map the default gateway's IP address to its own MAC address, silently intercepting traffic. DHCP snooping is already enabled on the switches. Which additional switch feature MOST directly stops this attack?
c: Dynamic ARP Inspection that validates ARP messages against the DHCP snooping binding table
BPDU Guard configured on all of the user-facing access ports
Port security limiting each access port to a single learned MAC address
Storm control rate-limiting broadcast traffic across the affected VLAN

q: A threat intelligence feed supplies a frequently updated list of malware command-and-control domains. The security operations team wants infected internal hosts to be automatically cut off from their controllers and simultaneously identified for cleanup. Which control BEST achieves both goals?
c: Block the current IP addresses of the malicious domains at the perimeter firewall
Configure the internal DNS resolvers to sinkhole the listed domains to a monitored internal address
Enable DNSSEC validation on all of the internal DNS resolvers
Increase resolver query logging and have analysts review the logs each week

q: A network architect must carry OSPF routing updates and multicast video between two data centers across the public Internet. A proof of concept using policy-based IPsec ESP tunnels fails because the multicast hello packets are never delivered. Which design BEST meets the routing and multicast requirements while preserving confidentiality?
c: Switch the IPsec tunnels from ESP to AH so the routing protocol traffic is permitted
Loosen the IPsec policy selectors so the multicast address ranges match the ESP tunnel
Replace IPsec with a plain GRE tunnel, which encapsulates multicast and routing protocols
Encapsulate the traffic in GRE or a virtual tunnel interface and protect that tunnel with IPsec ESP

q: After a VoIP rollout onto the existing converged LAN, call quality collapses into dropouts and delays whenever nightly backup jobs saturate the links. Management asks the security team which security property is threatened and what should be applied. What is the BEST answer?
c: Confidentiality is threatened; encrypt all of the voice streams with SRTP
Availability is threatened; apply quality-of-service policies that prioritize latency-sensitive voice traffic
Integrity is threatened; enable MACsec encryption on the switch uplinks
Confidentiality is threatened; move the phones onto a separate voice VLAN

q: A company permits employee-owned laptops on the corporate wireless network. Several malware outbreaks are traced to personal devices that authenticated with valid user credentials but were months behind on patches and ran no endpoint protection. Which control BEST reduces this risk while preserving the BYOD program?
c: Network access control that assesses device health at connection and quarantines noncompliant devices for remediation
WPA3-Enterprise authentication issuing unique per-user network credentials
Mandatory full mobile device management enrollment with corporate control of personal laptops
A policy prohibiting personally owned devices from all corporate networks

q: To speed up maintenance windows, a network engineer downloads switch operating system images from a fast third-party mirror site. The security architect is concerned that a tampered image could implant a persistent backdoor in the network fabric. Which practice BEST ensures the integrity and authenticity of images before installation?
c: Compare each image's file size and version string against the vendor's release notes
Scan every downloaded image with the enterprise antivirus engine before staging it
Obtain images through the vendor's official channel and verify the vendor's digital signature or published hash before deployment
Maintain configuration backups so any affected switch can be quickly restored after an incident

q: A penetration test demonstrates that any host on a data center VLAN can transmit crafted first-hop redundancy protocol advertisements with a higher priority, seize the virtual gateway role from the legitimate router pair, and intercept all outbound traffic. Which remediation BEST addresses this exposure?
c: Enable DHCP snooping so hosts cannot be handed a rogue default gateway address
Deploy Dynamic ARP Inspection on the VLAN to stop the gateway impersonation
Configure static ARP entries for the gateway address on every attached server
Enable authentication on the redundancy protocol and filter its messages arriving from host-facing ports

q: An enterprise is replacing ISDN trunks with SIP trunking to an Internet telephony provider. The architect wants a purpose-built element at the voice perimeter to hide internal telephony topology, validate and normalize SIP signaling, and drop malformed messages before they reach the call manager. Which component BEST fits this role?
c: A stateful perimeter firewall with the SIP and RTP port ranges opened through it
A session border controller that terminates and re-originates signaling and media at the edge
A VoIP-aware intrusion detection sensor attached to a switch monitoring port
End-to-end SRTP encryption between the internal phones and the provider

q: Sales staff returning from a trade show report that their phones received unsolicited messages over Bluetooth, and one employee found an unfamiliar device paired to his wireless headset. What is the BEST immediate guidance for traveling staff?
c: Set devices to non-discoverable, disable Bluetooth when it is not in use, and remove unrecognized pairings
Connect only to conference Wi-Fi networks that are protected with WPA3 encryption
Install the corporate VPN client and keep it enabled at all times while traveling
Rely on Bluetooth frequency hopping, which prevents nearby attackers from interfering

q: Branch office routers include LTE modems that automatically provide Internet connectivity when the primary WAN circuit fails. A design review notes that during failover, branch traffic reaches the Internet directly through the cellular carrier, bypassing the centralized firewall, proxy, and monitoring stack. What is the BEST design change?
c: Remove the LTE modems so that branch traffic can never bypass the security stack
Accept the exposure as-is because failover events are expected to be rare, brief, and difficult for attackers to time
Rely on the carrier-grade NAT applied by the cellular provider to shield the branch during failover
Force failover traffic through an encrypted tunnel back to the corporate security stack, or apply equivalent policy enforcement, before any Internet breakout

q: An organization exchanges sensitive email with key partners, relying on opportunistic STARTTLS between mail servers. An assessment shows an on-path attacker could strip the STARTTLS capability from the SMTP handshake, silently downgrading delivery to cleartext. Which measure BEST prevents this downgrade for mail exchanged with partner domains?
c: Publish a DMARC record with a reject policy for both of the domains
Deploy S/MIME certificates to every user at each partner organization so message bodies are encrypted end to end
Adopt MTA-STS or DANE policies so sending servers require authenticated TLS when delivering to the partner domains
Configure the mail servers to accept only TLS 1.3 cipher suites for SMTP sessions

q: A CISO has sponsored a program to segment a flat corporate network that has grown organically for a decade. The lead architect proposes immediately purchasing next-generation firewalls and drafting the VLAN plan. What should the program do FIRST?
c: Run a competitive procurement to select the segmentation firewall platform
Discover and document the applications, data flows, and interdependencies that will define the security zones
Deploy microsegmentation agents to all servers to begin enforcing workload isolation
Author a default-deny policy between the proposed zones so enforcement can start on day one

q: A retailer's entire store network falls within its payment card compliance scope because point-of-sale terminals share a flat network with security cameras, guest Wi-Fi, and back-office PCs, driving assessment costs up sharply. Which approach BEST reduces compliance scope while protecting cardholder data?
c: Isolate the cardholder data environment into tightly controlled segments and verify that other zones cannot communicate with it
Deploy IPsec encryption between all of the devices across the existing flat store network
Install intrusion detection sensors throughout the store networks to monitor for card data theft
Rebuild the point-of-sale terminals on hardened operating system images

q: A secure web gateway enforces acceptable-use policy and TLS inspection for managed laptops. Analysts notice a rising share of web traffic leaving on UDP port 443 that the gateway passes uninspected, as updated browsers prefer HTTP/3. Until the gateway natively supports the new protocol, what is the BEST way to retain policy enforcement?
c: Point the existing TLS inspection appliance at the UDP flows so they are decrypted like other web sessions
Steer the laptops to the enterprise DNS resolver so the encrypted traffic becomes visible again
Permit the UDP flows because the new protocol encrypts everything and is therefore inherently safe
Block outbound UDP port 443 at the egress so browsers fall back to inspectable TCP-based HTTPS

q: The certificate on a company's remote-access VPN gateway expired a week ago. Rather than renewing it immediately, the help desk has been instructing users to click through the browser and client warnings so they can keep working. What should concern the security manager MOST?
c: The expired certificate means the VPN sessions are no longer being encrypted in transit
Every remote user's password must be treated as compromised and reset before the certificate is renewed
Users are learning to bypass certificate warnings and would accept an attacker's forged certificate the same way
The expired certificate will appear as a repeat audit finding in the upcoming compliance review

q: A company is planning its first wireless network across three floors of a shared office tower, directly adjacent to a competitor's suite. Before selecting access point models and mounting locations, what should the project team do FIRST?
c: Purchase high-power access points to guarantee coverage in every corner of the space
Conduct a wireless site survey to map coverage needs, interference sources, and signal spill beyond the leased space
Configure WPA3-Enterprise authentication on all of the SSIDs that will be broadcast
Install wireless intrusion prevention sensors throughout the three leased floors

q: During an incident review, a hospital discovers that malware moved between virtual machines running on the same hypervisor host without ever being seen by the data center's physical intrusion prevention system, because the traffic never left the host's virtual switch. Which change BEST closes this visibility gap?
c: Introduce inspection at the virtualization layer, such as a virtual firewall or hypervisor-integrated controls governing VM-to-VM traffic
Upgrade the physical intrusion prevention appliance to a model with much higher throughput
Mirror the core switch uplinks to the intrusion detection system with a SPAN session
Route all inter-VM traffic out of the host and through the physical core so the existing appliances can inspect it

q: An audit of an IPv4-only monitored network finds that endpoints with dual-stack operating systems have been building automatic IPv6 transition tunnels, such as Teredo and 6to4, that reach the Internet encapsulated in ordinary IPv4 packets, invisible to the egress controls. What is the BEST response?
c: Deploy RA Guard and DHCPv6 snooping on the access switches to stop rogue IPv6 announcements
Create a perimeter firewall rule that blocks outbound UDP port 3544, the default port used by Teredo
Disable the IPv6 protocol stack on every endpoint through a group policy pushed across the enterprise
Use endpoint management to disable transition tunnels, filter protocol 41 and Teredo at the egress, and extend monitoring to IPv6

q: A data loss prevention investigation finds a workstation sending a steady stream of outbound ICMP echo requests with large, high-entropy payloads to a single external host — a tunneling tool exfiltrating data. The traffic passed the perimeter because outbound ping is permitted to anywhere. Which network control change MOST directly prevents a recurrence?
c: Block inbound ICMP echo requests from the Internet at the perimeter firewall
Add an intrusion detection signature that alerts on high-volume ping floods
Apply default-deny egress filtering that stops nonessential protocols such as outbound ICMP, and inspect what remains for anomalies
Rate-limit outbound ICMP at the perimeter so any tunneled transfer would take far longer to complete

q: A manufacturing plant's PLCs accept Modbus/TCP commands from engineering workstations and HMIs. The protocol carries no authentication, so any device that can reach the control segment can issue write commands to the PLCs, which cannot be upgraded or modified. Which compensating control BEST reduces the risk of unauthorized commands?
c: An industrial protocol-aware firewall between zones that permits only approved sources and explicitly allowed Modbus function codes and registers
Enabling TLS encryption on the Modbus service of each PLC to authenticate all connecting clients
Relying on the existing industrial DMZ that brokers all data exchange between the IT and OT networks
Installing antivirus agents on the engineering workstations and HMIs in the control segment

q: An audit of a Fibre Channel storage area network finds that any server attached to the fabric can discover and mount storage volumes belonging to other business units. Which combination of controls BEST enforces least privilege on the storage fabric?
c: Mutual CHAP authentication configured between all of the initiators and targets
Fabric zoning combined with LUN masking so each initiator sees only its assigned targets and volumes
Encryption of the data at rest across all of the storage arrays
Placing the storage traffic in a dedicated VLAN separated from user traffic

q: A security team must let business partners use a legacy application protocol through the perimeter, but wants each command inside the protocol validated and specific dangerous operations blocked. The current stateful packet filter can only track ports and connection state. Which technology BEST meets the requirement?
c: A circuit-level gateway relaying the partner sessions at the transport layer
A stateless packet filter configured with a strict access control list
A NAT gateway translating the partners' addresses at the network boundary
An application-level proxy that understands the protocol and filters individual commands

q: To cut latency, an operations team enables TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT) on the public API that processes customer payments. A security architect objects specifically for requests that change state. Which risk is the architect MOST likely raising?
c: Early data eliminates forward secrecy for the entire resumed TLS session
Enabling 0-RTT allows attackers to downgrade connections to older TLS versions
Early data is replayable, so a captured 0-RTT request could cause a non-idempotent operation like a payment to execute more than once
0-RTT resumption skips certificate validation, letting an impostor server accept the requests

q: A bank's mobile application connects to its API over TLS, validating the server certificate against the device's public trust store. The threat model includes a compromised public certificate authority issuing a fraudulent certificate for the bank's domain to enable interception. Which control BEST mitigates this threat within the app?
c: Purchase extended validation certificates for all of the bank's API endpoints
Pin the expected server certificate or public key in the application, with a managed process for rotation
Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security on the bank's API domain
Increase the RSA key length used by the API server certificates

q: An architect must place a gateway between internal clients and an untrusted network. Requirements state that internal hosts must never connect directly to external systems, that dozens of different application protocols must be supported without building a protocol-specific inspection module for each, and that per-packet payload inspection latency is unacceptable. Which technology BEST satisfies these requirements?
c: Application-level proxy
Stateful packet-filtering firewall
Circuit-level gateway
Next-generation firewall with deep packet inspection

q: A company's flat network has grown to 900 hosts on one subnet. Broadcast chatter is degrading performance, and any host can observe discovery traffic from every other host. Which change BEST addresses the problem?
c: Replace remaining hubs with switches throughout the network
Divide the network into routed subnets using VLANs and a layer 3 device
Insert transparent bridges between the busiest network sections
Add repeaters to strengthen signals across the long cable runs

q: A firewall administrator using stateless access control lists has been forced to permanently permit inbound traffic across wide high-numbered port ranges so that replies to outbound sessions can return. A reviewer flags this exposure. Which capability BEST eliminates the need for those standing inbound rules?
c: Stateful inspection that records outbound connections and dynamically permits only matching return traffic
ACL entries that match the TCP established flag on returning packets
An application-layer proxy deployed for every permitted protocol
Port address translation so replies are mapped to existing sessions

q: A nightly batch job transmits payroll files to a bank using FTP with a hardcoded account. A security assessment notes that both the credentials and the file contents cross the Internet in cleartext. Which remediation BEST resolves the finding?
c: Migrate the job to TFTP, which presents a smaller attack surface
Require a complex FTP password that is rotated every month
Move the FTP service to a non-standard port to evade sniffing
Migrate the transfer to SFTP using key-based authentication

q: A hotel provides wired guest Internet access with all rooms on one subnet. Guests have reported attacks originating from other guests' devices on the same network. Every guest still needs Internet access, and the hotel wants minimal administrative overhead. Which switch configuration BEST addresses the risk?
c: Configure private VLAN isolated ports so guest devices can reach only the upstream gateway
Enable DHCP snooping on all guest-facing switch ports
Create a separate routed VLAN for each guest room
Enable port security limiting each port to a single MAC address

q: A penetration test demonstrates that a laptop plugged into a user segment can form an OSPF adjacency with a core router and inject routes that redirect internal traffic through the attacker's machine. Which remediation BEST addresses the root cause?
c: Deploy RPKI route origin authorizations for the organization's prefixes
Replace OSPF with static routes on every router in the enterprise
Enable cryptographic authentication on OSPF adjacencies and set user-facing interfaces to passive
Block IP protocol 89 at the Internet perimeter firewall

q: A regulator requires that a plant's safety-instrumented system network have no technical possibility of receiving inbound network connections from corporate systems, yet process historian data must flow continuously to corporate analytics. Which design BEST satisfies both requirements?
c: An industrial DMZ with dual firewalls permitting only sessions initiated from the plant side
A unidirectional security gateway that replicates historian data to a corporate-side server
An air gap with operators carrying data out on encrypted removable media each shift
An IPsec tunnel from the historian to the analytics platform with mutual authentication

q: A SOC must detect unusually large outbound transfers and periodic beaconing across 200 branch offices. Full packet capture at every site has been rejected as cost-prohibitive and raising privacy concerns. Which approach BEST meets the detection goal within those constraints?
c: Deploy full-packet-capture appliances at each branch and retain thirty days of traffic
Install signature-based intrusion prevention sensors at every branch office
Review the headquarters firewall's denied-connection logs each morning
Export NetFlow/IPFIX records from existing branch routers to a central collector for behavioral analysis

q: External auditors need three weeks of access to two internal web applications. Their firm prohibits installing other companies' VPN client software on its laptops, and your policy requires least-privilege access for third parties. Which remote access approach BEST fits the situation?
c: A clientless TLS VPN portal with multifactor authentication publishing only the two applications
Ship the auditors corporate-managed laptops preloaded with the IPsec VPN client
Create local accounts on the applications and expose them directly to the Internet for the engagement
Issue the auditors a full-tunnel VPN client profile granting routed access to the internal network

q: A software company engages offshore contract developers. The contract requires that source code never be stored on devices outside company control, while developers still need responsive access to development tools. Which approach BEST satisfies the contractual requirement?
c: Ship developers company laptops protected with full-disk encryption
Build a site-to-site VPN and replicate the code repository to the outsourcer's network
Provide virtual desktops in the company data center so only screen output and input traverse the network
Install data loss prevention agents on the contractors' own workstations

q: A CISO discovers that project teams routinely coordinate with external partners through personal consumer messaging apps, sharing client data with no retention, audit, or administrative control. The business depends on fast partner communication. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Block the consumer messaging apps at the corporate firewall and refer violators for discipline
Deploy an approved enterprise collaboration platform with partner guest access and retention controls, then restrict the consumer apps
Publish an acceptable-use policy prohibiting business use of personal messaging apps
Route the consumer app traffic through a cloud access security broker for monitoring

q: A cloud team has grown to 40 virtual networks joined by full-mesh peering. An audit finds that any workload can reach any other with no traffic inspection between environments, including between development and production. Which architectural change BEST remediates the finding?
c: Enable flow logging on every virtual network and review the logs weekly
Deploy host-based firewalls on every compute instance in all 40 networks
Consolidate all workloads into a single large virtual network organized by subnets
Rebuild connectivity as a hub-and-spoke transit design that forces inter-network traffic through centralized inspection

q: Users near a competitor's office are repeatedly dropped from the corporate WLAN. Analysis shows forged deauthentication frames spoofing the access points' addresses. The WLAN uses 802.1X with a strong EAP method. Which control MOST directly prevents these disconnections?
c: Require protected management frames (802.11w) for all WLAN associations
Migrate to a stronger EAP method with longer client credentials
Filter the attacker's MAC address on all access points
Deploy wireless sensors to detect and locate deauthentication floods

q: Network devices across a campus send syslog to the SIEM over UDP port 514 through shared user networks. An assessment notes that log events can be read in transit, forged by any host, or silently lost. Which change BEST addresses all three issues?
c: Schedule log forwarding during off-peak maintenance windows
Generate hashes of the stored log files nightly on the SIEM
Forward syslog over TLS with mutual certificate authentication on a reliable transport
Relocate the SIEM collector into the same VLAN as the network devices

q: An architecture review labels the SFTP gateway in the screened subnet a bastion host. A junior engineer asks what that designation requires of the system. Which statement BEST describes the obligation?
c: It must run deception services designed to attract and study attackers
It must be hardened and stripped to a single purpose because it is directly exposed to untrusted traffic
It must have two network interfaces and route packets between the internal and external networks
It must be hidden behind address translation so external hosts cannot reach it

q: A retailer subscribes to an upstream volumetric DDoS scrubbing service, yet its web storefront was taken offline by an attack that held thousands of HTTP connections open with slow, incomplete requests while total bandwidth stayed low. What is the BEST addition to the defense?
c: Purchase additional scrubbing bandwidth from the upstream provider
Rate-limit inbound ICMP and UDP traffic at the network edge
Subscribe to geolocation feeds and block the attacking countries
Add application-aware protection enforcing connection timeouts and slow-request limits

q: To reduce certificate costs, an organization installed a single wildcard certificate for *.example.com, copying its private key onto 60 servers, several of which are operated by hosting partners. What is the MOST significant risk of this practice?
c: Compromise of any one server exposes a private key that can impersonate every service under the domain
The wildcard certificate forces every site onto the same weak cipher suites, degrading the encryption strength
Browsers will present trust warnings because wildcard certificates come from lower-assurance authorities
The certificate cannot be revoked before its natural expiration if misuse is ever discovered

q: An Internet-wide scan report shows 14 of a company's servers with remote desktop directly reachable from the Internet, and authentication logs show continuous password-guessing attempts. Which remediation BEST reduces the risk?
c: Move the remote desktop service to a non-standard port and enforce longer passwords
Remove direct exposure and require access through a VPN or remote desktop gateway with multifactor authentication
Configure account lockout after three failed authentication attempts
Deploy an intrusion detection sensor to alert on the password-guessing activity

q: A trading firm buys Internet service from two different ISPs for resilience. A single fiber cut during road construction severs both connections simultaneously; investigation reveals both providers' circuits enter the building through the same conduit. What is the BEST corrective action?
c: Contract with a third Internet service provider for additional capacity
Tune BGP timers and add bidirectional forwarding detection for faster failover
Require and validate physical path diversity, with circuits following separate routes and building entry points
Negotiate stricter availability service level agreements with financial penalties from both providers

q: During recurring attacks, a public web server's connection table fills with thousands of half-open TCP connections from spoofed source addresses while link bandwidth utilization stays low, making the site unreachable. Which control MOST directly counters this attack?
c: Route inbound traffic through an upstream volumetric scrubbing service
Increase server memory to support a much larger connection table
Block inbound ICMP echo requests at the network perimeter
Enable SYN cookies or SYN proxying so state is committed only after the handshake completes

q: An organization's Internet-facing SMTP gateway accepts messages from any external sender and forwards them to any external destination. Spammers have begun abusing it, and the company's mail servers now appear on public blocklists. What should be done FIRST?
c: Reconfigure the gateway to relay mail only for authenticated users and the organization's own domains
Contact the blocklist operators and request removal of the company's addresses
Publish SPF records for the organization's sending domains
Enable TLS encryption on all SMTP connections handled by the gateway

q: Auditors cannot attribute configuration changes on routers and switches because all network engineers share one local administrator account. The organization wants individual authentication, authorization of specific commands per role, and a full record of every command executed. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?
c: Migrate device management to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy
Deploy RADIUS with 802.1X authentication for the engineering staff
Centralized TACACS+ AAA with individual accounts, command authorization, and accounting
Create a unique local account for each engineer on every device

q: A security team observes that clients connecting to the company's web services often skip certificate revocation checks when the CA's OCSP responder is slow or unreachable, and that successful lookups reveal user browsing activity to the CA. Which change BEST improves revocation reliability and user privacy for these services?
c: Publish larger certificate revocation lists on a more frequent schedule
Enable OCSP stapling with must-staple so servers present a signed, current revocation proof in the handshake
Pin the services' certificates inside the client applications
Move the services to self-signed certificates to remove the CA dependency

q: A penetration tester connects a laptop to an active conference room network jack and, without authenticating, immediately captures periodic advertisements revealing the switch model, operating system version, management address, and VLAN details. Which hardening step BEST eliminates this information disclosure?
c: Enable port security to restrict the MAC addresses permitted on the jack
Administratively disable all unused switch ports in public areas
Require SSH instead of Telnet for all switch management sessions
Disable discovery protocols such as CDP and LLDP on user-facing access ports

q: A red team reports that its exploit passed the network intrusion prevention sensor by splitting the payload into overlapping IP fragments that the target operating system reassembled differently than the sensor expected. Which control BEST prevents this class of evasion?
c: Have the boundary device fully reassemble and normalize fragmented traffic before inspection
Block every fragmented IP packet at the perimeter firewall
Shorten the sensor's signature update interval from daily to hourly
Replace the inline sensor with a passive monitoring deployment

q: An e-commerce company's two authoritative DNS servers, hosted in a single data center, were saturated during a DDoS attack, making the company's sites unreachable even though the web servers stayed up. Which change would BEST improve the resilience of the DNS service against a similar future attack?
c: Increase the TTL values on all DNS records so resolvers cache answers longer
Deploy DNSSEC signing on the zone to authenticate responses sent to resolvers
Serve the zone from a geographically distributed anycast network of name servers
Move both authoritative servers to a higher-bandwidth link in the same facility

q: An ISP has deployed RPKI route origin validation, yet a security review notes that its long-lived eBGP peering sessions can still be torn down by an attacker who spoofs TCP reset packets or injects forged segments into the session. Which control BEST addresses this remaining risk?
c: Authenticate the peering sessions with TCP-AO and enforce GTSM TTL security checks
Create signed route origin authorizations covering every prefix the ISP originates
Deploy strict inbound prefix filters that reject invalid announcements from peers
Rely on BCP 38 source-address filtering to keep spoofed packets off the Internet

q: A penetration test of a legacy site-to-site VPN concentrator reports that it accepts IKEv1 aggressive mode with pre-shared keys, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to capture a hash derived from the PSK and attempt offline cracking. The device supports modern configurations. What is the BEST remediation?
c: Lengthen the pre-shared key substantially and rotate it on a quarterly schedule
Migrate the tunnels to IKEv2 using digital certificates to authenticate the gateways
Change the IPsec proposal from AH to ESP so that the key exchange is encrypted
Run the IKE service on a nonstandard UDP port so attackers cannot locate it

q: During an architecture review, a security manager finds that the corporate network relies entirely on a single perimeter firewall: once inside, any host can reach servers, management interfaces, and databases without further checks. Which secure design principle is MOST clearly violated?
c: Least privilege
Separation of duties
Economy of mechanism
Defense in depth

q: A hospital's Internet firewall must be patched monthly, but each reboot drops all active clinical sessions, so the operations team keeps deferring updates. The security manager wants patches applied on schedule without interrupting traffic. Which approach BEST satisfies both goals?
c: Schedule the patches during an announced 2 a.m. maintenance window each month
Deploy the firewalls as a high-availability pair with state synchronization and patch one node at a time
Distribute filtering to host-based firewalls on the clinical servers so the perimeter device matters less
Install a hardware bypass module so traffic keeps flowing while the firewall reboots

q: A marketing team retired a cloud-hosted campaign site but left the CNAME record shop.example.com pointing at the released cloud hostname. Weeks later, phishing pages appear at that subdomain with the company's legitimate domain in the address bar. Which practice would MOST effectively prevent a recurrence?
c: Make DNS record removal a required step in resource decommissioning and audit zones for entries referencing unclaimed external services
Sign the zone with DNSSEC so that resolvers can cryptographically verify every response they receive
Restrict zone transfers to authorized secondary servers so outsiders cannot enumerate the zone's records
Monitor certificate transparency logs for unexpected certificates issued on the company's subdomains

q: A cloud provider stretches tenant Layer 2 segments between hypervisors using VXLAN over its data center IP fabric. A design review notes that VXLAN itself provides no authentication or encryption, so any host able to inject UDP datagrams into the underlay could spoof a VTEP and insert frames into tenant networks. Which measure BEST mitigates this risk?
c: Assign each tenant a unique VXLAN network identifier to keep their segments separated
Block the VXLAN UDP port at the Internet perimeter firewalls so outsiders cannot reach it
Isolate the underlay so only hypervisor VTEPs can reach it and protect inter-VTEP traffic with IPsec
Use only private RFC 1918 addressing in the underlay so external hosts cannot route to the VTEPs

q: A logistics company plans a permanent private circuit to a major retail partner so order data can flow between their ERP systems. The network team is ready to order the circuit and configure routing. From a security governance standpoint, what should be completed FIRST?
c: Perform an authenticated vulnerability scan of the partner systems that will be reachable across the circuit
Install and configure a dedicated firewall pair to control traffic at the interconnection boundary
Exchange cryptographic keys with the partner and stand up a site-to-site IPsec tunnel across the circuit
Negotiate an interconnection security agreement documenting each party's responsibilities, required controls, and permitted data flows

q: An analytics platform in a company's virtual private cloud reads sensitive records from the provider's managed object storage service. A review finds this traffic exits through the VPC's Internet gateway to the storage service's public endpoint. Which change BEST reduces the exposure of this data path?
c: Route the traffic through a private endpoint for the storage service so it stays on the provider's internal network
Require TLS 1.3 with strong cipher suites for every API call made to the storage service
Send the traffic through a NAT gateway so the analytics subnet's addresses are never exposed
Restrict the storage bucket policy so it accepts requests only from the VPC's public IP range

q: A defense contractor must run network cabling carrying regulated data between two secured suites at opposite ends of a floor shared with other tenants. The program's accreditation requires that the physical cable path itself be protected against tampering and covert access, and rerouting is not possible. Which measure BEST satisfies the requirement?
c: Encrypt all traffic crossing the corridor with MACsec between the switches in each suite
Install the cabling in a protected distribution system of sealed, monitored conduit with tamper-evident carriers and periodic inspection
Replace the run with shielded twisted pair to prevent signal emanations from the cable
Replace the copper run with fiber optic cable because optical media cannot be tapped

q: A university's port-based firewall permits TCP 443 outbound for web browsing. The security team discovers peer-to-peer file sharing and unauthorized remote-desktop tools operating freely because they all tunnel over port 443. Which capability BEST restores the intended policy?
c: Deploy an intrusion prevention signature set covering known peer-to-peer exploits
Publish an acceptable use policy that explicitly bans the unauthorized tools
Enforce rules based on identified applications rather than ports using a next-generation firewall
Resolve the offending services' addresses and maintain IP blocklists at the perimeter

q: A security assessment of a branch office finds that every port on the access switches is active and assigned to the staff VLAN, although fewer than half are in use. Wall jacks in vacant cubicles and the public lobby are live. NAC deployment is budgeted for next year. What is the BEST interim measure?
c: Enable DHCP snooping on the access switches to control address assignment
Rely on the lobby cameras to deter anyone from plugging into the open jacks
Configure port security so that each access port learns and allows a single MAC address
Administratively disable the unused ports and assign them to an isolated, unused VLAN

q: An investigation reveals that a developer's docked laptop was connected to the wired corporate LAN while its Wi-Fi adapter was associated with the developer's personal phone hotspot, and traffic flowed on both interfaces. Web filtering and DLP saw none of the hotspot traffic. Which control MOST directly addresses this exposure?
c: Enforce endpoint configuration that blocks connecting to unmanaged networks while attached to the corporate LAN
Deploy 802.1X port authentication so that only corporate devices can use the wired network
Add personal hotspot SSIDs to the corporate wireless intrusion prevention system's containment list
Require that all corporate web traffic pass through the authenticated forward proxy

q: Facilities is deploying hundreds of Zigbee occupancy and temperature sensors reporting to gateways bridged onto the corporate network. A wireless assessment shows the mesh was commissioned with the vendor's published factory default network key, and the gateways permit new devices to join at any time. What is the MOST important remediation?
c: Upgrade the sensors to WPA3 so the mesh benefits from modern wireless encryption
Commission the mesh with unique keys replacing the vendor default and allow joining only during controlled enrollment windows
Reduce the sensors' transmit power so their signals do not reach beyond the building
Move the sensor gateways onto a dedicated VLAN isolated from corporate systems by ACLs

q: Sales staff frequently work from hotels and airport lounges on open wireless networks. The security team wants to ensure corporate laptop traffic cannot be intercepted or manipulated by others on those networks. Which measure BEST accomplishes this?
c: Instruct staff to connect only to wireless networks that display the official venue name
Configure the laptops to prefer networks secured with WPA3 whenever one is available
Require an always-on, full-tunnel VPN that blocks traffic until the encrypted tunnel is established
Rely on each website's HTTPS connection to protect the users' sessions from onlookers

q: During commissioning of a new branch network installed by a contractor, an internal review finds the switches and wireless controller still accept the manufacturer's default administrative password, which is printed in publicly available documentation. What should the security team require FIRST?
c: Enroll every device in the central logging and monitoring platform before go-live
Apply the latest vendor firmware updates to every switch and the wireless controller
Audit the contractor's remaining deliverables for similar deviations from the requirements
Replace the default credentials with strong, unique ones from the hardening baseline before production use

q: A regional bank's customers report fraud calls whose caller ID displays the bank's official phone numbers, and the complaints are eroding trust in legitimate outreach calls. The calls originate entirely outside the bank's telephone infrastructure. Which measure MOST directly addresses this spoofing?
c: Engage the carriers to implement STIR/SHAKEN attestation so downstream networks can verify calls claiming the bank's numbers
Publish a DMARC reject policy for the bank's domains so that spoofed messages are refused
Encrypt all of the bank's outbound call media with SRTP so conversations cannot be forged
Deploy a session border controller to conceal the topology of the bank's VoIP infrastructure

q: An audit finds that the senior network engineer can request, approve, and implement firewall rule changes alone, and several undocumented permissive rules are attributed to this account. No malicious intent is suspected. Which improvement should the security manager prioritize?
c: Revoke the engineer's firewall administration rights and reassign the duties to another administrator
Require rule changes to pass an independent approval workflow separating request, approval, and implementation
Configure the SIEM to raise an alert whenever the firewall rulebase is modified in any way
Contract an annual penetration test to identify overly permissive rules in the firewall estate

q: A security team wants early warning if any certificate authority, including ones the company has never done business with, issues a TLS certificate for the company's domains to an unauthorized party. Which approach provides this detection?
c: Publish CAA records listing the certificate authorities authorized to issue for the domains
Enable OCSP stapling with must-staple on all of the company's public web servers
Subscribe to monitoring of public Certificate Transparency logs for the company's domain names
Pin the company's server certificates inside its own mobile applications

q: A red team reports that whenever a Windows workstation mistyped a hostname, the workstation broadcast a name-resolution query that the team answered from a rogue machine, causing the victim to send authentication material to the attackers. Dozens of password hashes were captured this way in hours. Which remediation MOST directly eliminates this attack path?
c: Enforce longer, more complex passwords so that any captured hashes resist offline cracking
Deploy Dynamic ARP Inspection on all of the user access VLANs across the campus
Require DNSSEC validation on the internal resolvers so responses cannot be forged
Disable LLMNR and NetBIOS name resolution by policy so hosts rely solely on authoritative DNS

q: After a company placed its web farm behind a load-balancing reverse proxy, incident responders discovered that all web and application logs now record the proxy's IP address as the client for every request, making abuse investigations impossible. Which remediation BEST restores investigative capability?
c: Configure the proxy to forward the original client address, via X-Forwarded-For or PROXY protocol, for the servers to validate and log
Extend the retention period for the existing web and application server logs
Correlate the proxy's logs with the server logs by timestamp manually during each investigation
Enable verbose debug-level logging on all of the web servers behind the proxy

q: A research lab section prohibits radio-frequency transmissions because of sensitive instrumentation, yet scientists need wireless connectivity for mobile workstations within a single enclosed room. Which technology BEST fits these constraints?
c: Bluetooth Low Energy operating at its minimum transmit power settings
Li-Fi optical wireless networking confined by the room's walls
Wi-Fi 6E in the 6 GHz band configured for reduced transmit power
Standard Wi-Fi using directional antennas aimed away from the instruments

q: A company's VoIP deployment already encrypts call audio with SRTP, but a security review finds that SIP signaling crosses the network in cleartext, exposing calling patterns, extension numbers, and digest authentication exchanges to anyone capturing packets. Which control addresses this finding?
c: Strengthen the SRTP cipher suite protecting the media streams between the endpoints
Move all of the telephones onto a dedicated voice VLAN separated from data traffic
Protect the signaling channel by carrying SIP over TLS between phones and call servers
Mask calling-party details with a session border controller at the network edge

q: An abuse notice from an upstream provider states that a company DNS server is participating in reflection attacks against third parties: it answers recursive queries from any Internet address, returning large responses to victims whose addresses were forged in the requests. Block all inbound UDP port 53 traffic at the Internet perimeter
Report the source addresses observed in the queries to law enforcement
Restrict recursion so the server answers recursive queries only for authorized internal clients

q: A regional bank connects its branch offices to the data center over a carrier-provided MPLS network. Replace the MPLS circuits with site-to-site VPN tunnels routed over the public Internet

Obtain the carrier's SOC 2 report and formally accept the circuits as trusted transport

Enable registry lock on the domain and require multifactor authentication for registrar account access
